questions.q: What specific problem does a failover group solve that active geo-replication alone does not?
options: It manages a stable listener endpoint (a single DNS name) so the application never has to know which region is currently primary
It is the only way to replicate data across Azure regions at all
It eliminates the need for any secondary database to exist
It removes the possibility of any data loss during failover
questions.explain: Geo-replication replicates the data; a failover group adds the connection-endpoint management layer on top of it.

questions.q: With plain active geo-replication and no failover group, what has to happen after a manual failover for the application to keep working?
options: The application (or its connection string) has to be updated by hand to point at the new primary's actual server name
Nothing — the application automatically reconnects to the new primary with zero changes
The old primary database is permanently deleted
A brand-new Azure subscription must be created
questions.explain: Without a failover group's stable listener endpoint, the client has no way to know which server is now primary except being told directly.

questions.q: What are the two failover policy options for a failover group?
options: Manual (a DBA triggers it explicitly) or Automatic (triggered on its own, based on a grace-period policy)
Fast and Slow, with no other configuration
Only Automatic — manual failover is not supported by failover groups
Only Manual — automatic failover is not supported by failover groups
questions.explain: A failover group can be configured for manual failover (same control as geo-replication alone) or automatic failover governed by a grace period.

questions.q: Why does an automatic failover policy include a grace period instead of triggering the instant the primary looks unreachable?
options: To avoid an unnecessary failover being triggered by a brief, transient network blip rather than a real outage
Because Azure requires at least 24 hours before any failover can occur
The grace period has no real purpose and is purely cosmetic
Because automatic failover is otherwise instantaneous with zero configuration
questions.explain: The grace period trades a slightly slower automatic RTO for protection against reacting to a false alarm.

questions.q: How is a failover group actually created, and why not with a T-SQL statement?
options: Via PowerShell, the Azure CLI, or the Azure Portal — because a failover group is a server-level Azure resource, not a per-database T-SQL object
With a CREATE FAILOVER GROUP T-SQL statement run against the primary database
It cannot be created through automation at all, only by contacting Microsoft support
By running ALTER DATABASE SET PARTNER, the same syntax used for database mirroring
questions.explain: Failover groups are server-level resources managed through Azure tooling (PowerShell/CLI/Portal), not through T-SQL against the database.
